open_points.subject: Inspection/read surfaces (`surface` vs domain modules)
open_points.text: "Inspection. The read projections of every record ... are `surface`'s, reading through `store.read_records` and `store.page_records` ... the owning modules add no read operation for inspection alone." + candidate capabilities `slot_repair_view` (`functions`) and `read_trace` (`runs`).
open_points.question: Should inspection-style reads be built only in `surface` from generic store paging, or are `functions.slot_repair_view` and `runs.read_trace` required domain read APIs that `surface` calls?
options: `surface` alone assembles all inspect/read projections from `store` and domain modules expose no read APIs for inspection.
`surface` delegates some read projections to domain modules (`functions`, `runs`) and those APIs are part of State 3 ownership.
open_points.default_guess: Use `surface`+`store` only for inspection, and treat `slot_repair_view`/`read_trace` as non-inspection helpers or remove them.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution write ordering when operation outcomes and graph-side effects happen together
open_points.text: "The record that concludes an operation element ... is built and written by `effects` ... every other record ... is built and written by `runs`, which alone applies the order of A15 rule 1 to records written together. `effects` does not know `runs`."
open_points.question: When an operation-node conclusion causes additional non-executed records (for example transitive `upstream_failed`/`skipped_by_guard` conclusions), must they be written in one ordered batch, and which module owns that combined write?
options: `effects` writes only the operation element record; `runs` later derives/writes any additional records in a separate call.
`effects` returns outcome details and `runs` performs the single ordered trace-write batch including the operation record.
A shared store-level primitive writes a coordinated batch from both modules' intents.
open_points.default_guess: Let `effects` write only the operation element record, then `runs` writes derived records afterward.

open_points.subject: Startup spool cleanup decision and call order (`runs` vs `store`)
open_points.text: "Spools at start. Which ended runs no longer keep a spool is `runs`' decision ... `store` removes what `runs` names" and `store` owns "start-time removal of temporary files"; `surface` start order is "installation, store, sandbox probe, `in_flight` recovery, run recovery".
open_points.question: At startup, exactly when is the set of removable run spools determined and by whom, relative to store opening and recovery steps?
options: `store` computes removable spools itself during open/start cleanup.
`runs` computes removable spools after recovery scans and instructs `store` to remove them.
Startup has two cleanup passes: `store` temp cleanup at open, then `runs`-directed spool cleanup later.
open_points.default_guess: Do temp-file cleanup in `store` at open, then have `runs` determine removable run spools and call `store` to remove them after recovery.
